issues.description: The template's Stock.findStockIngredient method signature (findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive)) does not match the problem specification and the solution, which both expect findStockIngredient(String). Additionally, methods in the template (add, take) call findStockIngredient with a single String argument, causing a signature mismatch and leading to a compilation error. This mismatch will confuse students about the correct method to use and prevents them from implementing SealSaloon as described.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock class provide the single-argument method public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) as specified in the problem (or add an overload that delegates to the boolean version). Ensure all internal calls (add, take) use the single-argument signature so the template compiles and matches the UML and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a Stock.findStockIngredient(String) method (single String parameter), and the solution implements findStockIngredient(String) accordingly, but the template repository's Stock class exposes findStockIngredient(String, boolean) (an extra boolean parameter). This signature mismatch (parameter list difference) creates a mapping barrier: students reading the problem will expect a single-parameter method while the provided template forces a different method shape, causing confusion when implementing SealSaloon or following the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem specification and solution by changing the template Stock method signature to: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) — remove the boolean parameter — and adjust its implementation/usages accordingly so students see the same API described in the problem and implemented in the reference solution.
